clue.text: Iago cursed in dismay

indicators.note: the letters of the first two words are put in a new state, so 'in' signals they must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's villain swears in horror at how things have turned out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iago cursed' looks like a scene from Othello, but its ten letters are simply rearranged; 'in' is the thin signal for that.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismay someone is to dishearten them, the same as putting them off, a straightforward verb synonym.

clue.text: It divides the church, say, in Ireland, perhaps

indicators.note: say signals the word is to be spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: the passage running between the pews is the aisle

explanation.surface: Something splits the church, as in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: The church passage between pews sounds the same as the word for an island; 'perhaps' marks Ireland as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Ireland is an island, the Emerald one, so it is an example of the word for an island.

clue.text: It's regular trade practice

definitions.meaning: the regular patronage of a shop by its ...
an established habit or tradition

explanation.definitionFit: Custom is the business of regular buyers, and also a traditional practice or habit.

clue.text: Ruin the opening?

definitions.meaning: downfall or destruction
the act of unfastening, as of buttons or a knot

explanation.definitionFit: Someone's undoing is their ruin, and undoing a fastening is opening it.

clue.text: A pain in the stomach eased by treatment

indicators.note: in shows the answer sits inside the following words

explanation.surface: Stomach discomfort is relieved by medical treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'stomach eased'; 'by treatment' only completes the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache is a dull, continuing pain, a direct synonym.

clue.text: East politician bound to be exhausted

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament
bound means tied up

explanation.surface: An eastern politician tied up is worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhausted can mean drained or used up completely, as a tank is emptied.

clue.text: Timorous person, eager to get the skill

parts.note: fain is an old word meaning glad or willing
art means skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: A nervous person who longs to pick up an ability.
explanation.walkthrough: FAIN is an archaic word for eager or willing; 'to get' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A timid, cowardly person is called this, as in the saying about never winning a fair lady.

clue.text: Being bad-tempered he has to go over a bit

parts.note: to cross is to go over, as a road
a patch is a small piece or area

explanation.surface: A grumpy man has to go and check over a portion of work.
explanation.definitionFit: A crosspatch is an irritable, grumpy person, one being bad-tempered.

clue.text: Just show

definitions.meaning: just means equitable or even-handed
a show is an exhibition or fete, such as an agricultural one

explanation.definitionFit: Fair means just as an adjective, and as a noun it is a show or exhibition.

clue.text: All union members finished business for the day

definitions.meaning: a workplace where every worker must belong to the trade union
a shop that has shut its doors after trading

explanation.definitionFit: A closed shop is a union-only workplace; read literally it is a store that has stopped trading for the day.

clue.text: Game entangled in nets

indicators.note: things entangled are twisted out of order, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A game gets caught up in the nets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entangled' scrambles IN plus NETS; the nets fit the sporting picture neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis is a racket sport, an example of a game.

clue.text: Cutter for part of the quarter-deck

definitions.meaning: the hardest stone, used in tools that cut glass and rock
one of the four suits, each a quarter of a pack of cards

explanation.definitionFit: A diamond is used as a cutting tool, and diamonds are one suit, a quarter of a card deck.

clue.text: Possibly a good tryer? That's somewhat disparaging

indicators.note: possibly means the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Calling someone a good tryer is faint praise and rather insulting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges A GOOD TRYER; the surface rightly notes that 'good tryer' is a backhanded compliment.
explanation.definitionFit: Derogatory means belittling or disparaging, a close synonym.

clue.text: A battle in last war

parts.note: reads like a fight from the most recent war, but means the final battle at the end of the world

explanation.definitionFit: In Revelation this is the site of the final battle between good and evil at the end of days.

clue.text: Toys sold out round end of April

indicators.note: round shows one piece goes around the other
out suggests the letters are disordered
end of picks the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Toys sold out by late April.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SOLD to DOLS; 'round' wraps that around L, the last letter of April by 'end of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolls are figures children play with, an example of toys.

clue.text: He may call for you at an American hotel

definitions.text: He may call for you at an American hotel

parts.words: He may call for you at an American hotel
parts.note: reads as someone visiting a guest, but describes the US hotel page who calls out or fetches guests

explanation.definitionFit: A US hotel porter or page, who comes to the room or pages guests, is this.

clue.text: Comparatively bold material

parts.note: reads as a daring fabric, but is the metal whose name also means nerve or cheek

explanation.definitionFit: Brass is a metal alloy, and brass also means impudence or boldness, as in brass neck.

clue.text: It's planted soil or dug out of it

indicators.note: dug out of it suggests the letters are disturbed and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something sown in the ground or dug up from it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soil' is part of the picture only; the letters of OR DUG are rearranged, signalled by 'out of it'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gourd is a squash-like plant grown from seed, so it is something planted.

clue.text: Sheep drives

definitions.meaning: male sheep are tups
drives as in forces or pushes hard into place

explanation.definitionFit: Rams are male sheep, and rams is also a verb meaning forces or drives in.

clue.text: Rush job for a dressmaker

definitions.meaning: to rush is to dash or move quickly
a tapering tuck sewn into a garment to shape it

explanation.definitionFit: To dart is to rush, and a dart is a shaping tuck a dressmaker sews.

clue.text: Photo finish

parts.note: reads as a close race result, but means the shiny surface a print can be given

explanation.definitionFit: Photographs are printed with a matt or shiny surface coating, the shiny one being this.

clue.text: Ceases to be in love with someone and leaves

definitions.text: Ceases to be in love with someone
definitions.meaning: to lose one's liking for a person
departs or goes away

explanation.definitionFit: To go off someone is to stop liking them; to go off is also simply to leave.

clue.text: Surprise street art by the French

parts.note: taken as written
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Street art beside a French sign gives a shock.
explanation.definitionFit: To startle someone is to surprise or alarm them suddenly, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Professional dancers

parts.note: reads as ballet or ballroom performers, but means men paid to be dancing partners

explanation.definitionFit: Gigolos were men hired as escorts and dance partners, so they danced for money.

clue.text: Bird featured in pull out

definitions.meaning: British slang for a prison term, from rhyming slang bird-lime, time
to pull something out so it extends

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' suggests a feathered creature hiding in the word, but it is British slang for time in prison; 'featured in' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretch is slang for a prison sentence, like bird, and to stretch is to pull out.

clue.text: Former forward, should know better

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
pert means cheeky or forward

explanation.surface: A former cheeky child ought to know better by now.
explanation.definitionFit: A specialist is someone who ought to know more than others, so they should know better.

clue.text: Mary and Elizabeth were from Stroud

indicators.note: the queens were formed from this word, signalling its letters rearranged

parts.note: a market town in Gloucestershire, England, taken as written

explanation.surface: Two queens are said to come from a Gloucestershire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Stroud is a small English town in Gloucestershire; its letters rearrange into the royal house of Mary I and Elizabeth I.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary I and Elizabeth I were members of the royal house that ruled England from 1485 to 1603.

clue.text: Have some sense, charge a pound!

parts.note: a fee is a charge or payment
L stands for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Be reasonable and charge just a quid!
explanation.definitionFit: To feel is to experience by the sense of touch, so to have some sense.

clue.text: He falsifies accounts

parts.note: reads like a fraudulent bookkeeper, but means someone giving untrue stories

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who tells untrue accounts of events is a teller of falsehoods.

clue.text: How the descant will be broadcast

definitions.text: How the descant will be broadcast

parts.words: How the descant will be broadcast
parts.note: a descant is sung above the main melody, and broadcasting goes out by radio

explanation.definitionFit: Broadcasts go out by radio waves, and a descant sits above the tune, giving the phrase two senses.

clue.text: Cheat cornered on the board

definitions.meaning: to swindle or fleece someone
the chess piece that starts in a corner square

explanation.definitionFit: To rook is to swindle, and a rook is the chess piece standing in each corner at the start.

clue.text: Not a true origin of race perhaps

definitions.text: Not a true origin of race perhaps

parts.words: Not a true origin of race perhaps
parts.note: reads like ancestry, but means a race's beginning that must be rerun after a runner jumps the gun

explanation.definitionFit: When a runner leaves early the beginning of the race is void and must be repeated.
